messages:
Sam: Heads-up — we need to settle retention strategy for traces by environment and per-tenant overrides. Current defaults (7d hot / 30d cold) are blowing our monthly storage budget due to a few noisy customers.
Lee: Can you drop the latest numbers? How much is noise vs baseline?
Sam: Top 3 customers are ~42% of volume. Most of that is long-running debug traces + verbose spans. Full breakdown in the dashboard I linked earlier.
Neha: We already sample heavily in non-prod (x10), but production is mostly unsampled. Proposal: env-aware defaults + optional per-tenant caps and adaptive sampling.
Ben: Concern: if we cold-tier earlier, we lose searchability and span-level queries. Cold = compressed blobs, index pruned. How will alerts and diagnostics work? :thinking:
Marie: Thought: make cold store immutable compressed objects but keep a small index (trace_id -> location + minimal metadata) so we can still locate traces quickly. If a user requests a cold trace, we can promote it back to hot cache.
Alex: Promotion-on-query is fine but needs SLOs. Need to define expected latency for promoted traces vs hot reads. Also avoid DOS by bulk-promote requests.
Sam: Draft SLOs: hot read p95 < 150ms, promotion p95 < 2s, cold archive restore p95 < 30s (but we want to avoid restore in hot path). Open to numbers.
Neha: Ops: restoration failures are a thing. We need retry logic + circuit-breaker and metrics for restore latency/failures. Also quota impact if a tenant promotes thousands of traces at once.
Ben: For expensive tenants we could auto-apply aggressive sampling + size caps on spans and limit export retention. Maybe a per-tenant cost threshold that flips to higher sampling automatically.
Marie: Config example (rough):
```
# trace retention config (proposal)
trace_retention:
  prod: {hot: 7d, cold: 90d}
  staging: {hot: 2d, cold: 30d}
  dev: {hot: 1d, cold: 7d}
per_tenant_overrides: true
auto_throttle_threshold: 1000usd_per_month
auto_sampling_policy: {scale_down: 0.1, max_trace_size: 200KB}
```
Sam: Also consider tiered hot buckets: prod-critical (14d hot), prod-standard (7d), prod-lite (2d) — map by customer SLA.
Lee: How will billing work? If we promote a cold trace to hot, do we charge retrieval? Should count towards the tenant's monthly quota.
Alex: Yes - retrieval/promote should cost the same as hot storage + IO. Need to reflect in Console cost breakdown and alerts.
Neha: From infra side, cold stores are cheaper but slower (object store + compression). We can pre-warm by async promotion when query patterns indicate increased interest (recent time ranges, repeated user queries).
Ben: Query UX: team wants a hint in the Console saying "trace is in cold storage — click to restore (cost X, expected latency Y)". That reduces accidental restores.
Marie: Agreed. Also add a setting per-tenant: "allow_auto_promote_on_query" true/false. For regulated customers we'd forbid auto-promotion and require admin approval.
Sam: Important: tests. We need a staging runbook to simulate worst-case noisy tenant and cold promote storm. Add chaos test for mass-restores.
Neha: I'll add runbook skeleton: steps for throttling, temporary deny-promote, rollback.
Alex: Dev platform ask: expose a small API so frontend Console can surface promote cost and expected time. Something like: `POST /v1/traces/{id}/promote` -> returns job id + ETA.
Sam: Also add telemetry: metrics for promotes/sec, promote_failures, promote_latency_histogram, promoted_bytes, restore_bytes.
otel-bot: Exporter job for s3-archive finished: bucket="traces-archives-prod", prefix="2026/11/19/"  (info)
Ben: One more: indexing strategy. If we keep a tiny inverted index for cold, which fields? trace_id, service_name, start_ts, duration, error_flag, maybe a low-cardinality tag set. Anything else will bloat the index.
Marie: Yes keep index minimal. For deep search, we restore. Also consider pre-computing sampling-aware aggregates (error rates by service) to avoid restores for common dashboards.
Lee: When do we ship a proposal? Can we converge on numbers this week? I can pull cost projections for the proposed buckets.
Sam: Let's meet tomorrow 10am to align SLOs + per-tenant policy flow. I'll post an RFC after that with concrete configs and UI mocks. :thumbsup:
Neha: I'll prototype the promote API + metrics this week.
Ben: I'll work on Console copy and billing impact notes.
Marie: I'll draft the runbook and chaos tests.
Alex: Add me to the RFC review.
Sam: Thanks everyone — we'll iterate on the RFC.
